title: Free finite group action gives a finite etale torsor on its quotient locus
statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group acting admissibly on an integral excellent Noetherian scheme $C$, and let $U\subset C$ be a $G$-stable dense open on which the action is free on geometric points. Assume that the scheme quotient $q:C\to C/G$ exists, with invariant structure sheaf, that $C/G$ is Noetherian and that $q$ is finite. Put $V=q(U)$. Then $V$ is open, $U= C\times_{C/G}V$, and $U\to V$ is a finite etale $G$-torsor: it is finite etale, the $G$-action is simply transitive on every geometric fibre, and $V$ is the orbit-space quotient. If $C$ is separated and $U$ is dense, $V$ is dense and the induced extension of function fields is Galois with group $G$.

Conventions for the notions used here: [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-exc-excellent-ring], [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], [def-weil-etale-morphism], [def-sbc-normal-dominant-galois]. Here admissible means that every $G$-orbit is contained in an affine open; free on geometric points means $g\bar u=\bar u$ implies $g=1$ for every geometric point $\bar u:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to U$ [def-weil-geometric-point]. The invariant structure sheaf assumption is the canonical isomorphism $\mathcal O_{C/G}\simeq(q_*\mathcal O_C)^G$. Fibre products and separatedness have the meanings of [def-pc-fibre-product] and [def-weil-proper-morphism], respectively. The function field of an integral scheme $X$ is the stalk $\mathcal O_{X,\eta}$ [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk] of its structure sheaf at its generic point $\eta$ [def-sc-generic-point], the unique point whose closure is $X$; the extension of function fields induced by $q$ is the germ map $\mathcal O_{C/G,q(\eta)}\to\mathcal O_{C,\eta}$, where $q(\eta)$ is the generic point of $C/G$.

source.place: Expose IX 1.4, p. 132: the action is free over the complement of the vertical boundary; the quotient over that open is the finite Galois torsor used in condition (*).

proof.text: Write $Y=C/G$. For an affine open $D=\operatorname{Spec}A\subset Y$, finiteness makes $W=q^{-1}D=\operatorname{Spec}B$ affine, and the assumed invariant sheaf identifies $A=B^G$, with the given map $A\to B$ the inclusion. Use the action groupoid $R=\coprod_{g\in G}W\rightrightarrows W$: source is the identity on each component and target is $g$ on that component, with identity, inverse and composition supplied by the group laws. It is affine, namely $R=\operatorname{Spec}(\prod_G B)$. Both projections are finite locally free: for the source its algebra is the finite free module $B^{\oplus G}$; for the target each summand is twisted by an automorphism and hence is again free of rank one. The product algebra is finitely presented, using the finitely many orthogonal idempotents $e_g$ with $\sum e_g=1$; freeness gives flatness. Thus the finite, flat, locally finitely presented definition applies.

Apply [lem-a1-affine-groupoid-orbit-fibres] to the groupoid of Step 1. Its invariant ring is $B^G=A$, so $q$ is surjective over $D$, and its ordinary and geometric fibres there are single $G$-orbits. These statements hold on the affine cover of $Y$, hence globally. In particular, since $U$ is $G$-stable, every fibre meeting $U$ lies entirely in $U$.

source.place: Tag 03BL (lemma-points), applied to the action groupoid

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-closed-map-finite-fibres], $q(C\setminus U)$ is closed. Step 2 and surjectivity give $q(U)=Y\setminus q(C\setminus U)$ and $q^{-1}(q(U))=U$. Thus $V=q(U)$ is open. The pullback of the open subscheme $V\hookrightarrow Y$ is precisely the open subscheme on $q^{-1}V$: a morphism into $C$ factors through that open exactly when its composite into $Y$ factors through $V$. Hence $U\simeq C\times_YV$ with the given inclusions and projections. The restriction $p:U\to V$ is finite by base-change permanence.

source.place: Tag 01WN (lemma-finite-proper), Tag 01WL (lemma-base-change-finite); open-subscheme pullback by its universal property

proof.text: The action on $U$ is free on arbitrary test schemes. Indeed, let two locally constant maps $g,h:|T|\to G$ and $x:T\to U$ satisfy $gx=hx$. On each open-and-closed part where $(g,h)$ is constant, a nonempty part has a point $t$ and a geometric point above it, obtained by choosing an algebraic closure of $\kappa(t)$. Composing with $x$ gives a geometric point fixed by $h^{-1}g$, so $g=h$ on that part by the hypothesis. Thus $g=h$ everywhere, including when $T$ is empty. Consequently $(a,\operatorname{pr}_2):G\times U\to U\times_VU$ is a monomorphism: equality of its images first equates the $U$-maps, and then the preceding argument equates the $G$-maps. Reflexivity, symmetry and transitivity of its image are the identity, inverse and multiplication laws of $G$.

source.place: Tags 07S1 (definition-free-action), 07S2 (lemma-free-action); geometric-point test for a constant group

proof.text: For each affine open $D=\operatorname{Spec}A\subset V$, put $W=p^{-1}D=\operatorname{Spec}B$. Step 1 gives $A=B^G$ and finite locally free source and target for $R=G\times W$. Step 4 says that this action groupoid is an equivalence relation on every test scheme over $D$. Apply [lem-a1-finite-flat-affine-relation-quotient] with $S=D$. Its equalizer ring is exactly $B^G=A$, so its canonical quotient is the given $D$ and its canonical map is $p|_W$, by the affine spectrum correspondence. Therefore $p|_W$ is finite locally free and surjective, and $(g,w)\mapsto(gw,w)$ identifies $G\times W$ with $W\times_DW$. These identifications use the actual action maps and projections, so on overlapping opens their inverses agree by uniqueness of an inverse. They give a global isomorphism $G\times U\simeq U\times_VU$. Also $p$ is flat and locally of finite presentation: these are pointwise properties, verified on these affine neighbourhoods. Its finiteness was already established in Step 3.

source.place: Tag 03BM (proposition-finite-flat-equivalence), the affine argument behind Tag 07S7 (lemma-quotient-scheme)

proof.text: The single map $p:U\to V$ is an fpqc covering: it is flat by Step 5; over each affine open $D\subset V$, its affine inverse image $W$ maps onto $D$, so one affine piece suffices in the definition of an fpqc covering. After this base change, $p$ is the second projection $U\times_VU\to U$, identified in Step 5 with $\coprod_G U\to U$. This projection is etale: each source component maps by the identity, and on affine identity charts the ring map $B\to B$ is flat, finitely presented with zero relative differentials; equivalently its diagonal is the open-and-closed union of the equal-component parts. Thus it satisfies the etale definition. By [lem-galois-fpqc-descend-etale], $p$ is etale. Together with Step 3 this proves finite etaleness.

source.place: Tag 02VN (lemma-descending-property-etale); constant-group projection checked directly on identity charts

proof.text: Every geometric fibre of $p$ is nonempty by Step 2. Given two of its geometric points $x,y$, the kernel-pair isomorphism of Step 5 supplies a unique $g\in G$ with $gx=y$; hence the action is simply transitive. The restricted map is also the orbit-space quotient: it is surjective, its fibres are orbits, and it is closed because it is finite. If the inverse image of a subset $E\subset V$ is closed, then $E=p(p^{-1}E)$ is closed, proving the quotient topology. The invariant sheaf identity restricts from $Y$ to $V$ by evaluating on its open subsets. These are exactly the stated quotient and finite etale torsor clauses.

source.place: Tag 01WN (lemma-finite-proper); torsor kernel-pair criterion in spaces-properties.tex Tag 07S7

proof.text: The open $V$ is dense in $Y$. For any nonempty open $D\subset Y$, its inverse image under the surjection $q$ is nonempty open in $C$, hence meets the dense $U$; therefore $D$ meets $V$. Also $Y$ is integral: it is nonempty since $C$ is, and for every nonempty affine $D=\operatorname{Spec}A\subset Y$, Step 1 identifies $A$ with the subring $B^G$ of the domain $B$, since $q^{-1}D$ is a nonempty affine open of the integral $C$. This is precisely the affine definition of an integral scheme.

source.place: Tag 01OK (definition-integral); density by inverse images of opens

proof.text: Choose a nonempty affine $D\subset V$ and write $W=q^{-1}D=\operatorname{Spec}B$ and $D=\operatorname{Spec}A$, where $A=B^G$. By [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction], $L=k(C)=\operatorname{Frac}B$ and $K=k(Y)=\operatorname{Frac}A$, compatibly with $q$. The action on $L$ is $\rho(g)=(g^{-1})^*$ so that it is a left action despite contravariance of pullback. Its fixed field is exactly $K$: if $z=b/c\in L^G$ with $c\ne0$, put $d=\prod_{g\in G}\rho(g)(c)$. Then $d\in B^G\setminus\{0\}$ and $zd=b\prod_{g\ne1}\rho(g)(c)\in B$; as both $z$ and $d$ are invariant, $zd\in B^G=A$. Thus $z=(zd)/d\in\operatorname{Frac}A$. The reverse inclusion follows by fixing numerators and denominators. This proves the field identification directly without assuming that invariants commute with arbitrary base change.

source.place: Tag 09I3 (lemma-galois-over-fixed-field), applied after the elementary invariant-denominator calculation; function-field charts are Morphisms Tag 01RV

proof.text: The action $\rho$ on $L$ is faithful. If $\rho(g)$ is the identity, then $g$ fixes the geometric generic point $\operatorname{Spec}\overline L\to C$: the generic point is preserved by every automorphism and the induced map on its residue field $L$ is the identity. This geometric point lies in $U$, since every nonempty open of an integral scheme contains its generic point, so the freeness hypothesis forces $g=1$. Apply [lem-wf-finite-field-action-fixed-degree] to $L$ and this finite faithful action. With $L^G=K$ from Step 9 it gives a finite Galois extension $L/K$ of degree $|G|$. The natural homomorphism $G\to\operatorname{Aut}_K(L)$ is injective by faithfulness, while [lem-weil-pbc-finite-galois-fixed-field] gives $|\operatorname{Aut}_K(L)|=[L:K]=|G|$. An injection between these finite sets of the same cardinality is bijective. Thus this induced action identifies the Galois group with $G$, as required when $C$ is separated (the argument in fact does not need separatedness).

proof_origin.place: Tags 03BL (lemma-points) and 03BM (proposition-finite-flat-equivalence), affine constant-group specialization; descent.tex Tag 02VN and fields.tex Tags 09I3, 09I1. This expands the quotient assertion used in ILO Expose IX 1.4, printed pp.132--133, condition (*).
